title: GRASP responsibility patterns
idea: GRASP is a set of nine guidelines for deciding which class owns each responsibility, such as Information Expert, Creator, Controller and Pure Fabrication.
points: Information Expert: give a job to the class that holds the data.
Creator: class A creates B when A contains or aggregates B.
Controller: one non-UI class receives each system event and delegates.
Low Coupling and High Cohesion, from the last page, are GRASP guidelines too.

hero.title: Who owns each job at checkout

edges.label: checkout
edges.caption: Controller: the UI hands the system event to one class that is not UI code.

edges.label: new, add
edges.caption: The controller starts an `Order` and hands it the item; it does no maths itself.

edges.label: creates
edges.caption: Creator: `Order` contains its lines, so `Order` creates each `OrderLine`.

edges.label: save
edges.caption: Indirection: the controller talks to the `Orders` interface, not to a storage class.

edges.label: implements
edges.caption: Pure Fabrication: storage is not a domain idea, so an invented class does it.

edges.label: asks total
edges.caption: Information Expert: `Order` holds the lines, so it computes the total.

code.title: GRASP at checkout
code.caption: Every class got its job by asking one GRASP question: who has the data, who contains it, who receives the event?

walk.text: Controller: receives `checkout`, delegates every step, and does no arithmetic itself.
Creator: `Order` contains the lines, so it is the one that builds them.
Information Expert: `Order` holds the lines, so it sums them.
Each `OrderLine` is the expert on its own price times quantity.
Indirection: the controller depends on this interface, not on a storage class.
Pure Fabrication: an invented storage class. A database version could replace it (Polymorphism).

pitfalls: Do not put business rules in the controller; it should only receive and delegate.
Avoid one bloated controller that handles every system event; split controllers by use case.
Add a Pure Fabrication only for a clear job, not as a dumping ground.

quiz.q: After the two calls in `main`, this runs. What does it print?
quiz.why: `InMemoryOrders` keeps one list across calls, so this is the third save. `Order.total` asks each line: 340 times 2 is 680.

takeaway: Give each job to the class that has the data it needs.
